publicReleaseNotes:
Orbit 0.4.10 adds reviewed Zoom meeting preparation and attendance, clearer workflow activity, and more visible email permission during archive restore. It uses the existing rer 0.2.113 pin.

- **Prepare a Zoom meeting from its real details.** The installation owner can connect a Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app in Settings, with guidance for its meeting read scopes and webhook endpoint. A full operator reviews an exact scheduled, non-recurring meeting and chosen deal before attaching it. Its plan shows the Zoom link, attendees, saved agenda and preparation. A signed completion updates that meeting's activity and reads attendance metadata; the recap cites recorded facts. An internal follow-up still requires explicit review. Cancellation stops that meeting's preparation and open plan follow-ups. Zoom continues to own meeting creation and rescheduling. Orbit fetches no recording or transcript content, makes no transcript-based summary, and leaves unavailable attendance unresolved. Connection credentials stay out of exports; reconnect after restore. Live Zoom developer-account qualification and the complete cross-product buyer walk remain unproved.
- **Read what a workflow did.** Workflow activity names the triggering record, owner, task, notified teammates and field changes, with links to available records and readable before-and-after values. Undo shows the retained outcome. Exact diagnostics remain in technical details; this does not expand what Undo can reverse.
- **Review email permission before restoring an archive.** The restore preview names contacts returning as Do not contact and distinguishes archived holds from additional email stops retained by this installation or the archive. Restored contacts otherwise keep their archived permission, including an explicitly cleared hold. When an independent retained stop wins, contact history and audit explain its source, including a stop on another address of that contact. A new contact created from a captured meeting starts as Do not contact.
- **Receive one notice for a form enquiry.** The intended recipient gets the submission notice without a second NOW notice for that same intake. The notice names the contact; unrelated recipients and ordinary NOW events keep their notices.
- **Keep the maintained runtime current.** This release includes the already-landed rer 0.2.113 source refresh and Vite, Zod and Undici dependency fixes. The operations guide points to the current local run instructions.

Account proposals remain limited to selected written evidence and the existing three proposal types. Scheduled graph maintenance, transcripts, licensed enrichment and broader stakeholder inference remain incomplete. Workflow undo remains partial. Earlier erasure limitations remain: a former sponsor or approver can still appear by name in a colleague's timeline and audit rows, and an approver's name stays in the search index until it is rebuilt. These changes do not establish complete agent coverage, complete migration from another CRM or live-provider acceptance.

Update from 0.4.9 in place after stopping writes and taking a private backup. Apply the two pending migrations once, in order, before the new Worker serves: 0091 adds installation-local Zoom meeting, delivery and reviewed follow-up records; 0092 prevents a duplicate NOW notice for the form submission's intended recipient. Preserve the migration ledger and every already-applied migration; installations using intermediate migration names need their ledger and schema reconciled first. No new provider setting is required to retain existing features. Optional Zoom use needs the owner's Zoom app credentials, meeting read scopes and signed webhook setup. Older installations must first account for earlier pending migrations and release instructions.

Existing records and integrations retain their authority. Optional Zoom use requires the installation owner to connect a Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app with meeting read scopes and a signed webhook endpoint; credentials are excluded from archives and must be connected again after restore. Preserve all previously applied migrations and their ledger entries.

agentUpdateInstructions: Update from 0.4.9 in place; never reset or replace the installation. Stop local dev and hosted writes and take a private backup outside the checkout, using rer export locally or Records → Export archive when hosted. Check out v0.4.10 and run rer install with pinned Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and rer 0.2.113. Use rer setup locally or rer deploy --env-file .dev.vars.deploy when hosted. Preserve the migration ledger: apply only pending migrations 0091_zoom_meetings.sql and 0092_form_submission_notification.sql, once in order and before the new Worker serves or writes resume. Keep every already-applied migration and owner customization; migrations through 0090 belong to earlier releases and must not be replayed. Installations that applied intermediate candidates under earlier migration names need their ledger and schema reconciled before treating this as a routine upgrade; no automatic remapping is claimed. Older installations must first account for their earlier pending migrations and release-history instructions. No new provider setting is required to retain existing features. Optional Zoom use requires the installation owner’s Server-to-Server OAuth app, meeting read scopes and signed webhook setup; review the exact scheduled non-recurring meeting and deal before attachment. Orbit reads attendance metadata only, not recordings or transcripts, and Zoom remains responsible for meeting creation and rescheduling. Zoom credentials do not travel in archives; reconnect after restore. Preserve current email stops and explicit clear receipts. Review the restore preview and resulting contact Email permission before sending. Keep the prior mailbox-send and Pipedrive consent/reconnection requirements, Mailchimp webhook checks and owner confirmation for held deletion requests after reconnection or restore. Before resuming writes, check existing records, saved views, capture evidence and proposals, meeting plans and reviewed follow-ups, draft and scheduled mail, forms and notifications, workflow activity and integration settings. Retain the release-note limitations on graph maintenance, agent coverage, workflow undo, erasure and supported import scope.
